sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇy ṛtavaś caiva māsāḥ saṃdhyāḥ savatsarāḥ vainateyāḥ samudrāś ca kadrujāḥ pannagās tathā
english: The lunar mansions, the seasons, the months, the twilights, and the years; the sons of Vinatā, the oceans, and the serpents born of Kadrū—

sanskrit: śatadrūś ca vipāśā ca candrabhāgā sarasvatī sindhuś ca devikā caiva puṣkaraṃ tīrtham eva ca
english: the Śatadru and the Vipāśā, the Candrabhāgā and the Sarasvatī, the Sindhu and the Devikā, and the holy ford of Puṣkara—

sanskrit: gaṅgā mahānadī caiva kapilā narmadā tathā kampunā ca viśalyā ca karatoyāmbuvāhinī
english: the Gaṅgā, the great river, the Kapilā and the Narmadā, the Kampunā and the Viśalyā, and the water-bearing Karatoyā—

sanskrit: sarayūr gaṇḍakī caiva lohityaś ca mahānadaḥ tāmrāruṇā vetravatī parṇāśā gautamī tathā
english: the Sarayū and the Gaṇḍakī, and the Lohitya, that mighty stream, the Tāmrāruṇā, the Vetravatī, the Parṇāśā, and the Gautamī—

sanskrit: godāvarī ca veṇṇā ca kṛṣṇaveṇā tathādrijā dṛṣadvatī ca kāverī vaṃkṣur mandākinī tathā
english: the Godāvarī and the Veṇṇā, the Kṛṣṇaveṇā and the mountain-born streams, the Dṛṣadvatī and the Kāverī, the Vaṃkṣu and the Mandākinī—

sanskrit: prayāgaṃ ca prabhāsaṃ ca puṇyaṃ naimiṣam eva ca tac ca viśveśvarasthānaṃ yatra tad vimalaṃ saraḥ
english: Prayāga and Prabhāsa, and the holy Naimiṣa forest, and that abode of Viśveśvara where lies that spotless lake—

sanskrit: puṇyatīrthaiś ca kalilaṃ kurukṣetraṃ prakīrtitam sindhūttamaṃ tapodānaṃ jambūmārgam athāpi ca
english: and Kurukṣetra, renowned and dense with holy fords, the supreme Sindhu, the ground of austerity and almsgiving, and the Jambūmārga as well—

sanskrit: hiraṇvatī vitastā ca tathaivekṣumatī nadī vedasmṛtir vaidasinī malavāsāś ca nady api
english: the Hiraṇvatī and the Vitastā, and likewise the river Ikṣumatī, the Vedasmṛti, the Vaidasinī, and the river Malavāsā too—

sanskrit: bhūmibhāgās tathā puṇyā gaṅgādvāram athāpi ca ṛṣikulyās tathā medhyā nadī citrapathā tathā
english: the holy tracts of earth, and the Gate of the Gaṅgā as well, the streams of the sages, the sacred rivers, and the Citrapathā—

sanskrit: kauśikī yamunā sītā tathā carmaṇvatī nadī nadī bhīmarathī caiva bāhudā ca mahānadī mahendravāṇī tridivā nīlikā ca sarasvatī
english: the Kauśikī, the Yamunā, the Sītā, and the river Carmaṇvatī, the river Bhīmarathī and the Bāhudā, that great stream, the Mahendravāṇī, the Tridivā, the Nīlikā, and the Sarasvatī—

sanskrit: nandā cāparanandā ca tathā tīrthaṃ mahāhradam gayātha phalgutīrthaṃ ca dharmāraṇyaṃ surair vṛtam
english: the Nandā and the Aparanandā, and that ford, the Great Lake, then Gayā and the ford of the Phalgu, and the Dharmāraṇya frequented by the gods—

sanskrit: tathā devanadī puṇyā saraś ca brahmanirmitam puṇyaṃ trilokavikhyātaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śivam
english: and the holy river of the gods, and the lake fashioned by Brahmā, sacred, famed throughout the three worlds, auspicious, the remover of every sin—

sanskrit: himavān parvataś caiva divyauṣadhisamanvitaḥ vindhyo dhātuvicitrāṅgas tīrthavān auṣadhānvitaḥ
english: the Himavān, that mountain endowed with divine herbs, the Vindhya whose flanks are bright with minerals, rich in fords and abounding in healing plants—

sanskrit: merur mahendro malayaḥ śvetaś ca rajatācitaḥ śṛṅgavān mandaro nīlo niṣadho darduras tathā
english: the Meru, the Mahendra, the Malaya, and the Śveta heaped with silver, the Śṛṅgavān, the Mandara, the Nīla, the Niṣadha, and the Dardura—

sanskrit: citrakūṭo 'ñjanābhaś ca parvato gandhamādanaḥ puṇyaḥ somagiriś caiva tathaivānye mahīdharāḥ diśaś ca vidiśaś caiva kṣitiḥ sarve mahīruhāḥ
english: the Citrakūṭa and the collyrium-hued mountain, the Gandhamādana, the holy Somagiri, and all the other upholders of the earth, the quarters and the intermediate quarters, the soil, and all that grows from it—

sanskrit: viśvedevā nabhaś caiva nakṣatrāṇi grahās tathā pāntu vaḥ satataṃ devāḥ kīrtitākīrtitā mayā
english: the All-Gods, the firmament, the lunar mansions, and the planets—may these deities, named and unnamed by me, ever protect you all.

sanskrit: kīrtayāno naro hy etān mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ stuvaṃś ca pratinandaṃś ca mucyate sarvato bhayāt sarvasaṃkarapāpebhyo devatāstavanandakaḥ
english: The man who recites these names is freed from all his sins; praising and rejoicing in them, the one who delights in the praise of the deities is delivered from every fear and from all the sins of confusion.

sanskrit: devatānantaraṃ viprāṃs tapaḥsiddhāṃs tapodhikān kīrtitān kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvapāpapramocanān
english: After the deities, I shall now proclaim the renowned brāhmaṇas, perfected through austerity and abounding in penance, who release one from every sin.

sanskrit: yavakrīto 'tha raibhyaś ca kakṣīvān auśijas tathā bhṛgvaṅgirās tathā kaṇvo medhātithir atha prabhuḥ barhī ca guṇasaṃpannaḥ prācīṃ diśam upāśritāḥ
english: Yavakrīta and Raibhya, Kakṣīvān the son of Uśij, Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, then Kaṇva, the mighty Medhātithi, and Barhin endowed with every virtue—these have taken their stand in the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: bhadrāṃ diśaṃ mahābhāgā ulmucuḥ pramucus tathā mumucuś ca mahābhāgaḥ svastyātreyaś ca vīryavān
english: In the auspicious southern quarter dwell the greatly blessed Ulmuca and Pramuca, the high-souled Mumuca, and the valiant Svastyātreya.

sanskrit: mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putras tathāgastyaḥ pratāpavān dṛḍhāyuś cordhvabāhuś ca viśrutāv ṛṣisattamau
english: And the majestic Agastya, son of Mitra and Varuṇa, and Dṛḍhāyu and Ūrdhvabāhu, those two most eminent and renowned sages.

sanskrit: paścimāṃ diśam āśritya ya edhante nibodha tān uṣadguḥ saha sodaryaiḥ parivyādhaś ca vīryavān
english: Learn now of those who flourish, resting in the western quarter: Uṣadgu together with his brothers, and the valiant Parivyādha—

sanskrit: ṛṣir dīrghatamāś caiva gautamaḥ kaśyapas tathā ekataś ca dvitaś caiva tritaś caiva maharṣayaḥ atreḥ putraś ca dharmātmā tathā sārasvataḥ prabhuḥ
english: the sage Dīrghatamas, Gautama, and Kaśyapa, the great seers Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, the righteous son of Atri, and the mighty Sārasvata.

sanskrit: uttarāṃ diśam āśritya ya edhante nibodha tān atrir vasiṣṭhaḥ śaktiś ca pārāśaryaś ca vīryavān
english: Learn now of those who flourish, resting in the northern quarter: Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Śakti, and the valiant son of Parāśara—

sanskrit: viśvāmitro bharadvājo jamadagnis tathaiva ca ṛcīkapautro rāmaś ca ṛṣir auddālakis tathā
english: Viśvāmitra, Bharadvāja, and Jamadagni likewise, Rāma the grandson of Ṛcīka, and the sage son of Uddālaka—

sanskrit: śvetaketuḥ kohalaś ca vipulo devalas tathā devaśarmā ca dhaumyaś ca hastikāśyapa eva ca
english: Śvetaketu and Kohala, Vipula and Devala, Devaśarman and Dhaumya, and Hastikāśyapa too—

sanskrit: lomaśo nāciketaś ca lomaharṣaṇa eva ca ṛṣir ugraśravāś caiva bhārgavaś cyavanas tathā
english: Lomaśa and Nāciketa, and Lomaharṣaṇa as well, the sage Ugraśravas, and Cyavana of the line of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: eṣa vai samavāyas te ṛṣidevasamanvitaḥ ādyaḥ prakīrtito rājan sarvapāpapramocanaḥ
english: This, O king, is the foremost gathering, made up of sages and gods, which I have proclaimed to you—the deliverer from every sin.

sanskrit: nṛgo yayātir nahuṣo yaduḥ pūruś ca vīryavān dhundhumāro dilīpaś ca sagaraś ca pratāpavān
english: Nṛga, Yayāti, Nahuṣa, Yadu, and the valiant Pūru, Dhundhumāra and Dilīpa, and the majestic Sagara—

sanskrit: kṛśāśvo yauvanāśvaś ca citrāśvaḥ satyavāṃs tathā duḥṣanto bharataś caiva cakravartī mahāyaśāḥ
english: Kṛśāśva and Yauvanāśva, Citrāśva and the truthful one, Duḥṣanta and Bharata, that emperor of mighty fame—

sanskrit: yavano janakaś caiva tathā dṛḍharatho nṛpaḥ raghur naravaraś caiva tathā daśaratho nṛpaḥ
english: Yavana and Janaka, and the king Dṛḍharatha, Raghu, that best of men, and the king Daśaratha—

sanskrit: rāmo rākṣasahā vīraḥ śaśabindur bhagīrathaḥ hariścandro maruttaś ca jahnur jāhnavisevitā
english: Rāma the hero, slayer of the rākṣasas, Śaśabindu, Bhagīratha, Hariścandra and Marutta, and Jahnu attended by the daughter of Jāhnavī—

sanskrit: mahodayo hy alarkaś ca ailaś caiva narādhipaḥ karaṃdhamo naraśreṣṭhaḥ kadhmoraś ca narādhipaḥ
english: Mahodaya and Alarka, and the king Aila, Karaṃdhama, best of men, and the king Kadhmora—

sanskrit: dakṣo 'mbarīṣaḥ kukuro ravataś ca mahāyaśāḥ mucukundaś ca rājarṣir mitrabhānuḥ priyaṃkaraḥ
english: Dakṣa, Ambarīṣa, Kukura, and Ravata of great renown, the royal sage Mucukunda, and Mitrabhānu the kindly—

sanskrit: trasadasyus tathā rājā śveto rājarṣisattamaḥ mahābhiṣaś ca vikhyāto nimirājas tathāṣṭakaḥ
english: and king Trasadasyu, Śveta the most eminent royal sage, the renowned Mahābhiṣa, king Nimi, and Aṣṭaka—

sanskrit: āyuḥ kṣupaś ca rājarṣiḥ kakṣeyuś ca narādhipaḥ śibir auśīnaraś caiva gayaś caiva narādhipaḥ
english: Āyu, the royal sage Kṣupa, and the king Kakṣeyu, Śibi the son of Uśīnara, and king Gaya—

sanskrit: pratardano divodāsaḥ saudāsaḥ kosaleśvaraḥ ailo nalaś ca rājarṣir manuś caiva prajāpatiḥ
english: Pratardana, Divodāsa, Saudāsa lord of Kosala, Aila, the royal sage Nala, and Manu the Lord of Creatures—

sanskrit: havidhraś ca pṛṣadhraś ca pratīpaḥ śaṃtanus tathā kakṣasenaś ca rājarṣir ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ
english: Havidhra and Pṛṣadhra, Pratīpa and Śaṃtanu, the royal sage Kakṣasena, and others who have not been named one by one—

sanskrit: mā vighnaṃ mā ca me pāpaṃ mā ca me paripanthinaḥ dhruvo jayo me nityaṃ syāt paratra ca parā gatiḥ
english: may there be for me no obstacle, no sin, and no adversaries; may victory be ever steadfast for me, and in the world beyond, the supreme goal.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tūṣṇīṃbhūte tadā bhīṣme paṭe citram ivārpitam muhūrtam iva ca dhyātvā vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ nṛpaṃ śayānaṃ gāṅgeyam idam āha vacas tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Bhīṣma had fallen silent, like a figure painted upon a canvas, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī, having pondered for a moment, then spoke these words to the recumbent king, the son of Gaṅgā:

sanskrit: rājan prakṛtim āpannaḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvaiḥ pārthivaiś cānuyāyibhiḥ
english: "O king, Yudhiṣṭhira, the lord of the Kurus, has regained his composure, together with all his brothers and the princes who follow him.

sanskrit: upāste tvāṃ naravyāghra saha kṛṣṇena dhīmatā tam imaṃ purayānāya tvam anujñātum arhasi
english: He waits upon you, O tiger among men, together with the wise Kṛṣṇa; it is fitting that you grant him leave to return to the city."

sanskrit: evam ukto bhagavatā vyāsena pṛthivīpatiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ sahāmātyam anujajñe nadīsutaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the venerable Vyāsa, the lord of the earth, the son of the river, gave Yudhiṣṭhira leave together with his counselors.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ madhuraṃ tataḥ śāṃtanavo nṛpaḥ praviśasva puraṃ rājan vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: And the king, the son of Śaṃtanu, then spoke to him sweetly: "Enter the city, O king; let the fever of your mind depart.

sanskrit: yajasva vividhair yajñair bahvannaiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ yayātir iva rājendra śraddhādamapuraḥsaraḥ
english: Offer sacrifice with rites of many kinds, abounding in food and rich in well-earned gifts to the priests, O lord of kings, like Yayāti, with faith and self-restraint going before you.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmarataḥ pārtha pitṝn devāṃś ca tarpaya śreyasā yokṣyase caiva vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: Devoted to the dharma of the warrior, O Pārtha, gratify the ancestors and the gods; you shall be joined with good fortune—let the fever of your mind depart.

sanskrit: rañjayasva prajāḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtīḥ parisāntvaya suhṛdaḥ phalasatkārair abhyarcaya yathārhataḥ
english: Bring delight to all your subjects, console the people of your realm, and honor your well-wishers with fitting rewards, each according to his due.

sanskrit: anu tvāṃ tāta jīvantu mitrāṇi suhṛdas tathā caityasthāne sthitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ phalavantam iva dvijāḥ
english: May your friends and well-wishers live in your shelter, my son, even as the twice-born find shelter beneath a fruit-laden tree standing in a sacred place.

sanskrit: āgantavyaṃ ca bhavatā samaye mama pārthiva vinivṛtte dinakare pravṛtte cottarāyaṇe
english: And you must come to me at the appointed time, O prince, when the maker of day has turned back and the northern course of the sun has begun."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu kaunteyaḥ so 'bhivādya pitāmaham prayayau saparīvāro nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Saying "So be it," the son of Kuntī saluted the grandsire and set out with his retinue for the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya gāndhārīṃ ca pativratām saha tair ṛṣibhiḥ sarvair bhrātṛbhiḥ keśavena ca
english: Placing Dhṛtarāṣṭra at the head, with Gāndhārī faithful to her lord, together with all those sages, with his brothers and with Keśava—

sanskrit: paurajānapadaiś caiva mantrivṛddhaiś ca pārthivaḥ praviveśa kuruśreṣṭha puraṃ vāraṇasāhvayam
english: and with the townsfolk and country-folk and the aged counselors, the prince, O best of the Kurus, entered the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kuntīsuto rājā paurajānapadaṃ janam pūjayitvā yathānyāyam anujajñe gṛhān prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, the son of Kuntī, having honored the people of the town and the countryside as was right, dismissed them to their homes.

sanskrit: sāntvayām āsa nārīś ca hatavīrā hateśvarāḥ vipulair arthadānaiś ca tadā pāṇḍusuto nṛpaḥ
english: And the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, consoled the women whose heroes were slain, whose lords were slain, with abundant gifts of wealth.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣikto mahāprājñaḥ prāpya rājyaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ avasthāpya naraśreṣṭhaḥ sarvāḥ svaprakṛtīs tadā
english: Consecrated and having gained the kingdom, the deeply wise Yudhiṣṭhira, that best of men, then set all his subjects firmly in their places.

sanskrit: dvijebhyo balamukhyebhyo naigamebhyaś ca sarvaśaḥ pratigṛhyāśiṣo mukhyās tadā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Receiving the foremost blessings from the brāhmaṇas, the chief warriors, and the townsmen on every side, that best of the upholders of dharma—

sanskrit: uṣitvā śarvarīḥ śrīmān pañcāśan nagarottame samayaṃ kauravāgryasya sasmāra puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: the illustrious bull among men, having passed fifty nights in that finest of cities, called to mind the appointed time of the foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa niryayau gajapurād yājakaiḥ parivāritaḥ dṛṣṭvā nivṛttam ādityaṃ pravṛttaṃ cottarāyaṇam
english: Seeing that the sun had turned and the northern course had begun, he set forth from the City of the Elephant, surrounded by his officiating priests.

sanskrit: ghṛtaṃ mālyaṃ ca gandhāṃś ca kṣaumāṇi ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ candanāgarumukhyāni tathā kālāgarūṇi ca
english: Clarified butter, garlands and perfumes, garments of fine linen, choice sandalwood and aloe, and black aloe-wood besides—

sanskrit: prasthāpya pūrvaṃ kaunteyo bhīṣmasaṃsādhanāya vai mālyāni ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: the son of Kuntī sent on ahead for the honoring of Bhīṣma, together with precious garlands and jewels of many kinds.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya gāndhārīṃ ca yaśasvinīm mātaraṃ ca pṛthāṃ dhīmān bhrātṝṃś ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Placing at his head Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the renowned Gāndhārī, and his mother Pṛthā, the wise bull among men, with his brothers—

sanskrit: janārdanenānugato vidureṇa ca dhīmatā yuyutsunā ca kauravyo yuyudhānena cābhibho
english: followed by Janārdana and the wise Vidura, by Yuyutsu and by Yuyudhāna, O lord, the Kaurava—

sanskrit: mahatā rājabhogyena paribarheṇa saṃvṛtaḥ stūyamāno mahārāja bhīṣmasyāgnīn anuvrajan
english: surrounded by a great train of kingly splendor and praised, O great king, set out, leading after him the fires for Bhīṣma's rite.

sanskrit: niścakrāma purāt tasmād yathā devapatis tathā āsasāda kurukṣetre tataḥ śāṃtanavaṃ nṛpam
english: He went forth from that city even as the lord of the gods would go, and then on Kurukṣetra he came upon the king, the son of Śaṃtanu—

sanskrit: upāsyamānaṃ vyāsena pārāśaryeṇa dhīmatā nāradena ca rājarṣe devalenāsitena ca
english: attended by the wise Vyāsa the son of Parāśara, and by Nārada, O royal sage, and by Devala and Asita—

sanskrit: hataśiṣṭair nṛpaiś cānyair nānādeśasamāgataiḥ rakṣibhiś ca mahātmānaṃ rakṣyamāṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: and by the other kings who had survived the slaughter, gathered from many lands, and that great soul guarded all around by his protectors.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ vīraśayane dadarśa nṛpatis tataḥ tato rathād avārohad bhrātṛbhiḥ saha dharmarāṭ
english: Then the king beheld him lying upon his bed of a hero, and the King of Dharma alighted from his chariot together with his brothers.

sanskrit: abhivādyātha kaunteyaḥ pitāmaham ariṃdamam dvaipāyanādīn viprāṃś ca taiś ca pratyabhinanditaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī then saluted the grandsire, that subduer of foes, and the brāhmaṇas led by Dvaipāyana, and he was greeted in return by them.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhir brahmakalpaiś ca bhrātṛbhiś ca sahācyutaḥ āsādya śaratalpastham ṛṣibhiḥ parivāritam
english: With the officiating priests, who were like Brahmā himself, and with his brothers and with the imperishable Kṛṣṇa, he approached the one who lay upon the bed of arrows, encircled by sages—

sanskrit: abravīd bharataśreṣṭhaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kauravya śayānaṃ nimnagāsutam
english: and the King of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, together with his brothers, O Kaurava, spoke to that best of the Bharatas, the recumbent son of the river:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'haṃ nṛpate namas te jāhnavīsuta śṛṇoṣi cen mahābāho brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: "I am Yudhiṣṭhira, O king; homage to you, son of Jāhnavī. If you can hear me, O mighty-armed one, tell me—what may I do for you?

sanskrit: prāpto 'smi samaye rājann agnīn ādāya te vibho ācāryā brāhmaṇāś caiva ṛtvijo bhrātaraś ca me
english: I have come at the appointed time, O king, bringing your fires, O lord; the teachers and the brāhmaṇas, the officiating priests, and my brothers are here—

sanskrit: putraś ca te mahātejā dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ upasthitaḥ sahāmātyo vāsudevaś ca vīryavān
english: and your son, the mighty-splendored Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, stands present with his counselors, and the valiant Vāsudeva as well.

sanskrit: hataśiṣṭāś ca rājānaḥ sarve ca kurujāṅgalāḥ tān paśya kuruśārdūla samunmīlaya locane
english: And the kings who survived the slaughter, and all the people of the Kuru lands—behold them, O tiger of the Kurus; open wide your eyes."

sanskrit: yac ceha kiṃ cit kartavyaṃ tat sarvaṃ prāpitaṃ mayā yathoktaṃ bhavatā kāle sarvam eva ca tat kṛtam
english: "Whatever was to be done here, all of it has been accomplished by me; just as you bade me at the time, all of it indeed has been done."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu gāṅgeyaḥ kuntīputreṇa dhīmatā dadarśa bhāratān sarvān sthitān saṃparivārya tam
english: Thus addressed by the wise son of Kuntī, the son of Gaṅgā beheld all the Bhāratas standing gathered around him.

sanskrit: tataś calavalir bhīṣmaḥ pragṛhya vipulaṃ bhujam oghameghasvano vāgmī kāle vacanam abravīt
english: Then Bhīṣma, the wrinkles of his brow trembling, raising his mighty arm, the eloquent one with a voice like the roar of flooding storm-clouds, spoke these timely words:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā prāpto 'si kaunteya sahāmātyo yudhiṣṭhira parivṛtto hi bhagavān sahasrāṃśur divākaraḥ
english: "By good fortune you have come, O son of Kuntī, with your counselors, Yudhiṣṭhira; for the blessed maker of day, the thousand-rayed one, has indeed turned upon his course.

sanskrit: aṣṭapañcāśataṃ rātryaḥ śayānasyādya me gatāḥ śareṣu niśitāgreṣu yathā varṣaśataṃ tathā
english: Fifty-eight nights have now passed for me as I have lain upon the keen-pointed arrows, and they have seemed to me as long as a hundred years.

sanskrit: māgho 'yaṃ samanuprāpto māsaḥ puṇyo yudhiṣṭhira tribhāgaśeṣaḥ pakṣo 'yaṃ śuklo bhavitum arhati
english: This holy month of Māgha has now arrived, O Yudhiṣṭhira; a third part of it remains, and this fortnight ought now to be the bright one."
